notes: A hub chip means 'every train that calls at filterCrs', fetched server-side via Darwin filterCrs/filterType=to.
absorbs = printed destinations that disappear from the picker because the hub chip covers them.
A printed destination NOT in absorbs keeps its own chip AND its trains also appear under the hub chip.
Hub chips carry no operator suffix — several operators may call at the hub.

Live-probed 4 Sep 2026 (docs/jim-brief-fb51-west-of-england.md and the PR) with scripts/probe-uk-board.mjs --filter-crs=BRI: Bath Spa filtered to calls-at-BRI returned Gloucester, Weston-super-Mare, Bristol Temple Meads and Cardiff Central (12 trips); Westbury filtered to calls-at-BRI returned Bristol Temple Meads, Gloucester and Cardiff Central (7 trips). Every westbound train from Bath/Westbury runs via Temple Meads, so riders on this corridor anchor on Bristol rather than the eventual terminus.

Weston-super-Mare was not in the brief's proposed candidate list (Cheltenham Spa, Avonmouth and Severn Beach were, in its place) but the live BTH-filtered board actually showed it and did not show the other three — per the brief's own rule ('if the filtered board contains a terminus, it is a candidate; if it doesn't, it isn't'), Weston-super-Mare is included and Cheltenham Spa/Avonmouth/Severn Beach are not. Flagged for Tim's explicit sign-off in the PR since it departs from the proposed table.

Do NOT add hubs at Bristol Temple Meads, Gloucester, Chepstow or Taunton (brief, 4 Sep 2026): Bristol Temple Meads and Gloucester are themselves fan-out termini/hubs, not through-stations that need anchoring; Chepstow and Taunton's boards reach Bristol only on some services and their chips are recognisable termini in their own right.
